mappings.note: Names water vapour, a component of the atmosphere. Not C-SST1.1, because no instrument or measurement is involved.
Names meteorology as the systematic study behind forecasting - the discipline of observation rather than a fact about the air. Not LO-3 for that reason.
Recall of a temperature scale, i.e. a measurement convention. Grouped with the Celsius and Fahrenheit items rather than with LO-3 explanations.
'Ambient temperature' is the temperature of the surrounding air, a property of the atmosphere. Not C-SST1.1, because the term describes the air rather than the thermometer.

Recall of the IMD motto, whose content is the sun-driven cycle that produces rain. Filed with the other two motto items under the atmospheric-process outcome, since the frame has nothing for the institution itself.
Names the rain gauge - an instrument item. Not LO-3, which takes precipitation as a phenomenon.
Millimetres as the unit of rainfall is a measurement convention, like the millibar item. Not LO-3, since rain itself is not being described.
Compares pressure at sea level and on a summit - the vertical structure of the atmosphere. Not C-SST1.1, because no barometer is mentioned.
Names the barometer. An instrument item, distinct from the pressure-behaviour items that carry LO-3.
The millibar as the display unit for pressure is a measurement convention. Not LO-3, which is kept for how pressure actually varies.
'Acclimatise' names the body's adjustment to a new climate, which is people living with their climate. Not LO-4, because no region is located.
Names the wind vane from its pointer and tail - instrument identification. Not LO-3, because wind as a process is not at issue.
Names the anemometer from its rotating cups. Instrument identification, the companion to the wind-vane item.
Defines humidity as water vapour in the air - atmospheric composition. Not C-SST1.1, which carries the hygrometer.
Names relative humidity as the percentage of the air's maximum vapour capacity - a property of the air. Not C-SST1.1, since the term is conceptual rather than instrumental.
Names the hygrometer. Instrument item, deliberately separated from the two humidity-concept items above.
Names the weather station as the place where instruments are brought together - observation infrastructure. Not LO-3.
Expands the abbreviation AWS - again observation infrastructure. Not LO-6, because no hazard context appears in this item, unlike the Sikkim glacial-lake station.

The Loo is a named hot, dusty wind of a particular part of India, so the item ties a weather regime to a region. Not LO-3, because it is not the mechanism of wind that is asked but where this wind belongs.

Explains that weather is confined to the troposphere because that layer holds the water vapour and the activity - reasoning about atmospheric structure. Not LO-1, which is used for the items that merely name the layer.

Warm air expanding and cold air contracting to give a deeper tropical troposphere is structure explained by cause. Not LO-4, because the tropics and poles are used as thermal contrasts, not as regions to locate.

Why standard units are needed so readings can be compared between places - measurement practice. Not LO-5: the Chennai and Kashmir example appears, but the answer is about avoiding subjective comparison, not about how those people live.

Two examples of animal behaviour read as weather signs - traditional observation, grouped with the other weather-lore items. Not LO-6, because the answer settles on expected rain rather than on a flood to prepare for.
Pine cones described as natural humidity indicators, i.e. as a way of reading the air. Not LO-3, which was given to the companion item that asks which environmental factor drives the cone.
Distinguishes two kinds of thermometer by their range and purpose - instrument comparison. Not LO-3, because body temperature is not an atmospheric property.
The arithmetic of the daily temperature range - a derived measurement. Same lane as mean daily temperature, not LO-3.
The funnel-and-calibrated-cylinder principle of a rain gauge is instrument mechanics. Not LO-3, since rainfall as a phenomenon is not explained.
A shorter, thinner column of air above explains falling pressure with height - atmospheric structure. Not C-SST1.1, because no measurement is being taken.
Breathlessness at altitude is the human body responding to thin air, which is the people-and-environment outcome. Not LO-3: the thin air is the premise, and the body's difficulty is the answer.
Defines a depression as a marked low-pressure system - atmospheric structure and vocabulary. Not LO-6, because the item stops before any warning or preparation.

Why pressure is worth measuring covers both the forecasting craft (C-SST1.1) and the timely warnings for storms and cyclones that the answer ends on (LO-6). Either alone would drop half the expected answer.
Explains how the vane's tail turns the pointer into the wind - instrument function. Not LO-3, because the item is about the device, not about why wind blows.
Rotating cups counted over time to give km/h - instrument function, the twin of the wind-vane item. Not LO-3 for the same reason.
Coastal Kochi against inland Jaipur is the geographical distribution of humid and dry conditions. Not LO-3, because the item compares places rather than defining humidity.
How ambient humidity slows evaporation is an atmospheric-moisture mechanism. Not LO-5, because no human consequence is required here.
Two humidity figures are given and the learner must reason about evaporation rate - the mechanism, not the geography. Not LO-4, because Delhi and Kochi supply numbers rather than regions to place.
Humidity control in museums and food industry is a weather element governing human work. Not C-SST1.1, since the hygrometer is not what the question asks about.
The advantage of an AWS - continuous unattended sensing - is about observation technology. Not LO-6, because no hazard setting is given in this item.
How meteorologists turn instrument records into patterns and forecasts is the practice of observation and analysis. Not LO-3, because no atmospheric property is explained.
